The above guarantee cards were distributed personally to each voters in public places and in their homes while campaigning in Uttar Pradesh, Tamil Nadu Karnataka, Bangalore and other important States. It is very very interesting to note that the Guarantee Cards were duly signed by the Party President and their images were also printed on the Cards and to be filled by the voters and to be submitted to the nearest Post Office for opening their accounts. In 1975 Raj Narain had filed a similar Petition before the EC and Allahabad HC against Indira Gandhi for booth capturing and misusing State Machinery for winning elections. The Complaint was allowed and Indira Gandhi was disqualified and she was directed by the Court to be arrested which subsequently resulted in proclamation of Emergency in India. We may not know what will happen to the present petition which is pending before the Supreme Authorities, however if the petition is allowed then there will be far reaching consequences. Question: Is it possible for a court to issue an interim order without hearing the opposing party?
Answer: Yes it is definitely possible to obtain an ad hoc interim orders from the court before hearing on the other side but, subject to certain important conditions as laid down under orders XXXIX, Rule 1&2 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Once if you convince the court by filing an affidavit before the court furnishing all the details of the case, then you may get the favourable orders. Remember, once you get the orders in your favour then you must comply with other orders under CPC. If you fail to comply with the orders then the interim orders will stand vacated or upon application of the other side they will seek vacating the interim orders. Remember, it is very tough to get the favourable orders and it is equally tough to defend the orders subsequently when the opposite side appears before the court.

Question: How do you describe the abrogation of Article 370 on 5th August 2019 and the subsequent challenges by the petitioners in the court?

On August 6th, 2019 President issued a proclamation, CO 273 putting the Rajyasabha’s recommendation into effect. Immediately all the clauses of 370 ceased to operate. This means Special Status granted to J&K was removed. On August 9th 2019 Parliament passed Reorganisation Act, 2019, bifurcating State of J&K into two distinct states as J&K and Ladakh coming under the Union’s jurisdiction of India. Immediately the matter reached SC and the petitioners challenged the abrogation of 370 Special Status of J&K. First the matter came up before CJI Gogoi and later on befor CJI Ramana but, couldn’t be heard. Now it was heard before Constitutional five Bench judges, consisting of CJI, Justice SK Kaul, BR Gavai, Sanjeev Khanna and Surya Kant. The lead advocate Kapil Sibal contends that the 370 is a permanent provision specially designed for J&K and it cannot be removed. The Modi government has removed it due to political reasons as it has promised in it’s manifesto in 2019 that if it comes back to power it will abrogate the special status given to J&K. Sibal further says that the abrogation was done unconstitutionally because it was done in haste without the concurrence and recommendation from the J&K legislative assembly. Further he says that the dissolution of the J&K assembly and declaration of President rule was also unconstitutional. J&K is very special in itself and it cannot be compared with other states of India because it is totally separate disconnected geographically and culturally. India cannot claim it in any way - unfortunately this man is the member of Rajyasabha and he was also minister in UPA government. What should we expect from this guy? There were many other advocates who appeared for the petitioners and more or less they campaigned the same points in their arguments. The day the matter reached Rajyasabha and the way it was debated in the upper house one should see the speech of Amit Shah - it was so terrific which made my skin tingling with goosebumps to see.

AG went on further to argue that for example this Hon’ble Court enjoys Autonomy, but at the same cannot have Sovereignty and similarly the case with J&K matter.
